headline: IIT Mandi launches ‘Science on Wheels’ in Himachal Pradesh for school students
content: The Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Mandi has introduced the ‘Science on Wheels’ programme in Himachal Pradesh to encourage practical science education among school students, in collaboration with a university and an NGO. The Himachal Pradesh segment of the initiative was launched on October 17 at IIT Mandi Campus School in the presence of the institute's director, Laxmidhar Behera, an official said on Monday. The programme has been designed for students from Classes 6 to 12. Under this initiative, taken in partnership with Plaksha University and the Igniting Dreams of Young Minds (IDYM) Foundation, each school will receive around six hours of interactive learning, covering four key themes, namely space technology, robotics, sustainability and water filtration. Also Read | One in 5 Indian college students is already an entrepreneur: IIT Mandi’s GUESSS India 2025 report Supported by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, the programme aims to help students from rural areas understand how scientific topics taught in classrooms are experimented with and applied in real-life cases. Having already reached more than 7,500 students across 70 schools in Chhattisgarh and Punjab, the initiative now plans to cover 50 schools across Mandi, Kullu, Bilaspur, Hamirpur and Kangra districts in Himachal Pradesh. Following its launch, the team started its activities in Mandi, visiting Government Senior Secondary Schools in Badog, Baggi (K), Bari Gumanu, Batheri and Deori. The director said that the initiative can help build greater interest in science among children and encourage them to come up with futuristic technology in India. (With inputs from PTI)

headline: IIT Mandi launches ‘Science on Wheels’ to reach 50 schools across Himachal Pradesh
content: The Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Mandi, in collaboration with Plaksha University and the Igniting Dreams of Young Minds (IDYM) Foundation, has launched the ‘Science on Wheels’ programme in Himachal Pradesh to promote practical science education among school students, particularly those in rural areas. The initiative aims to cover 50 schools across Mandi, Kullu, Bilaspur, Hamirpur and Kangra districts. According to a press release issued by the Ministry of Education, the programme’s Himachal Pradesh segment was launched on October 17 at IIT Mandi [https://news.careers360.com/iit-mandis-guesss-india-2025-report-over-20-pc-indian-college-students-have-started-business] Campus School. The initiative is supported by the Department of Science and Technology (DST [https://news.careers360.com/dst-award-vaibhav-fellowship-22-indian-origin-scholars-collaborate-indian-institutes]), Government of India, through the National Council for Science and Technology Communication (NCSTC). The programme is designed for students in Classes 6 to 12 and offers around six hours of hands-on learning at each school. Activities are organised around four themes: space technology, robotics, sustainability and water filtration. Also read At 7 IITs, 1,495 reserved SC, ST, OBC faculty posts vacant; IIT Kharagpur alone has 710, reveals RTI data [https://news.careers360.com/iit-kharagpur-kgp-roorkee-bhu-ropar-1495-sc-st-obc-faculty-vacancy-7-iits-jodhpur-patna-tirupati-quota-rti-data-student-suicide] SCIENCE ON WHEELS EXPANDS ACROSS HIMACHAL SCHOOLS Following its launch, the Science on Wheels team began visiting schools in Mandi district. The initial visits covered government senior secondary schools in Badog, Baggi (K), Bari Gumanu, Batheri and Deori. The initiative aims to help students connect classroom lessons with practical experiments and develop scientific curiosity, rational thinking, creativity and innovation. The programme has previously reached more than 7,500 students through 70 schools in Chhattisgarh and Punjab, according to the Ministry of Education’s press release. It will now expand its activities to schools across Himachal Pradesh in the coming weeks. IIT MANDI DIRECTOR HIGHLIGHTS SCIENCE EDUCATION Speaking at the launch event, IIT Mandi Director Laxmidhar Behera said the initiative could help develop an interest in science among school students and encourage them to contribute to India’s technological development. Behera said, “Science on Wheels is a great initiative. We need to develop an interest in science amongst our children as they are the future of an Atmanirbhar Bharat (self-reliant India).” He added, “With the help of Science on Wheels, not only will we be able to instill interest in learning science within them, but these children could be the people who will come up with futuristic technology such as the fMRI machine and the Atomic Force Microscope in India, provided we do something more than just demonstrating science to them.” Deshraj Sharma, principal of IIT Mandi Campus School, also welcomed the initiative. Sharma said, “You are educating children about science in areas where even the sight of such scientific equipment and using it is an unusual opportunity for them. Thus, by doing so you are widening their horizons of thoughts and giving new opportunities to them for the future. It is indeed a noble project.” ROCKET LAUNCH SHOWCASES SCIENCE IN ACTION A live hydro rocket launch was one of the key attractions at the inauguration ceremony. The activity demonstrated scientific concepts related to force, pressure and motion, allowing students to connect classroom learning with real-world applications. One student at IIT Mandi Campus School said the activity changed how they viewed science. “It was amazing seeing the rocket launch live!” the student said. The launch event was also attended by Surya Prakash Upadhyay, chairperson of the School of Humanities and Social Sciences at IIT Mandi; Rahul Vaish, dean of faculty at IIT Mandi; and Shaily Mahendra of the University of California [https://news.careers360.com/iit-madras-global-research-foundation-opens-first-us-centre-in-california-to-boost-deep-tech-innovation-ecosystem], Los Angeles, who is working as an international environmental expert at IIT Mandi. Also read IIT Bombay scraps stricter cheating rules, restores original ‘student-friendly’ norms after campus suicide [https://news.careers360.com/iit-bombay-student-suicide-revert-original-exam-cheating-rules-iitb-senate-meeting-caught-chatgpt-ai-btech-engineering-protests] The project is led by Rucha Joshi, principal investigator at Plaksha University. The team also includes Harshad Kulkarni of IIT Mandi, Shashank Tamaskar of Plaksha University, Ratnesh Mishra, president of the IDYM Foundation, and Srijita Chkraburty, visiting assistant professor at Plaksha University, Mohali. The IDYM Foundation is an official Space Tutor of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) [https://news.careers360.com/isro-communication-media-scholar-india-world-top-2-percent-scientists-list-bangalore-sikkim-manipal-central-university-tamil-nadu]. The programme will continue with school visits across Himachal Pradesh, aiming to make practical science education more accessible to students in remote areas.

headline: Maharashtra Sugarcane Farmers Protest Ethanol Policy, Demand Relief
content: MAHARASHTRA FARMERS Thousands of sugarcane farmers joined a 185-km bike rally led by Raju Shetti of the Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana through almost all the major towns of Kolhapur district in Maharashtra on October 25. They were pressing for a first instalment of Rs.4,500 per tonne of cane and a higher minimum selling price (MSP) for sugar. The rally was part of an ongoing protest over eight demands, which also include a ban on ethanol imports and financial relief on sugar factory loans. The response to the rally surprised sugar mill managements and both the State and Central governments. For them, the protest is no longer “ignorable”. Farmers’ organisations in mainly western and southern Maharashtra and north Karnataka have been protesting for the past six weeks. The first of the eight demands is a higher MSP for sugar and ethanol. The MSP of sugar is Rs.31 per kg, while the fair and remunerative price (FRP) of cane is Rs.3,650 per tonne. That leaves the sugar industry with a direct loss of Rs.550. To offset such losses, the government introduced several schemes, including blending ethanol with petrol. But the scheme has not rescued the industry: the promised procurement of ethanol by oil marketing companies (OMCs) fell from 60 per cent in 2018 to 26-27 per cent in 2025. Maharashtra’s sugar mills built ethanol capacity of 396-424 crore litres, yet the OMCs procured only 36 per cent of it. These figures relate to ethanol from B-heavy molasses. Frontline reported on the ethanol crisis in August. https://frontline.thehindu.com/the-nation/maharashtra-sugar-mills-ethanol-policy-economy-crisis/article71317029.ece The situation has since worsened. In August and September, retail sugar prices rose to Rs.68-75 per kg, and sugar consumption is higher during the festive season. To rein in prices, the Union government on August 20 allowed the duty-free import of 1 million tonnes of raw sugar until October 31. The deadline has now been extended to December 31. The OMCs issue tenders for the period from November 1 to October 31 the following year. The latest tender, issued on October 16 by the five state-owned OMCs, seeks about 11 billion litres of ethanol but excludes ethanol made from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup, and B-heavy molasses, following directions from the Union government. Sugar mills that had B-heavy molasses ethanol ready are now in difficulty. Of Maharashtra’s 210 sugar mills, 121 have installed ethanol plants, and another 32 direct distilleries make ethanol from sugar syrup or B-heavy molasses. Maharashtra’s sugar industry will face losses of almost Rs.7,000 crore, the farmers’ side says. In a letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Shetti, a former Lok Sabha MP and once an alliance partner of the BJP at the Centre as well as in the State, wrote: “The government must step in to ensure the survival of the sugar industry. It should hike the sugar MSP to Rs.50 per kg.” Reacting to the decision to stop procuring ethanol made from sugar syrup or B-heavy molasses, he said: “We thought the government wanted to help the already deteriorating sugar industry. But here, the government seems to be against the sugar industry. By importing duty-free raw sugar and now banning procurement of B-heavy molasses-based ethanol, the government seems to have decided to finish off the cooperative sugar industry of India.” Drought, early crushing and a widening protest Drought in the State has added to the farmers’ distress. Sugar recovery from cane has reportedly fallen by 1.5 percentage points: a mill that once got 12 kg of sugar from 100 kg of cane now gets only 10.5 kg. Crushing costs are rising with inflation while the yield falls, which hurts farmers and mills alike. With retail sugar prices rising, the Maharashtra government asked mills to begin crushing on October 15, almost a fortnight before the regular start of the season. The organisation called for a “Stop Work” protest at mills against the order. An early start means crushing immature cane, which lowers recovery by around 1.5 to 2 per cent. In a drought year, cane is already drier, and harvesting has begun with immature cane. “Farmers will face almost 2 per cent loss in recovery in such a situation. Maharashtra’s sugar mills are mostly cooperative, meaning farmers are the real owners of the mills. How will farmers or these mills survive if the government continues to take decision after decision against the interests of farmers and mills?” asked Shetti. Farmers’ organisations are also demanding direct subsidies. “To compensate for the loss of income caused by multiple factors such as the ethanol procurement decision, drought, and premature crushing, the government should consider Rs.500 per tonne direct subsidy to farmers,” says a charter of demands submitted by the farmers. In Karnataka, farmers called for a protest in front of Union Minister Pralhad Joshi’s house in Hubli and began a march from Kittur Chennamma Circle in Hubli on September 30. They have temporarily suspended the protest after a committee headed by Prof. Ramesh Chand was appointed to review the demands. Earlier, in Maharashtra, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis met all the stakeholders of the industry on March 24 and assured them that he would speak to Union Cooperation Minister Amit Shah and Prime Minister Modi. Nothing has changed on the ground since then. Nearly 50 lakh farmers in the State grow sugarcane, and almost 10 lakh cane cutters are linked to the industry. Cane billing for farmers in 2024-25 was Rs.28,000 crore, and for cutters Rs.10,000 crore. The sugar industry’s annual turnover is Rs.50,000-60,000 crore, making it Maharashtra’s single largest agri-based industry. The crisis has built up over the years, and Frontline reported on it in April, showing how deeply it was affecting the industry. https://frontline.thehindu.com/politics/maharashtra-sugar-mills-financial-crunch/article70896997.ece Until then, the issue was confined to the files of sugar mills and the government. Now farmers have taken to the streets in Kolhapur, where Shetti’s October 25 rally covered almost all the major towns of the district. Who is Tukaram Mundhe and why is he trending? Who is Tukaram Mundhe and why is he trending? Tukaram Mundhe, FDA Commissioner and Maharashtra’s controversial crusader, is taking on food and pharma giants and becoming a hero in the eyes of the public. headline: Shimla-Bilaspur-Dharamshala highway opened for light vehicles
content: Shimla/Bilaspur (HP), Oct 27 (PTI) The Shimla-Bilaspur-Dharamshala National Highway, which had been closed for repair following road subsidence earlier in the day, has been opened to light vehicles, officials said on Tuesday. The key road connects the capital Shimla to the state’s nine districts. The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) had closed the stretch in the morning for all vehicles, an official spokesperson said in a statement. The NHAI and the office of the Bilaspur Superintendent of Police followed the development with an advisory, suggesting alternative routes. Earlier, the police suggested motorists headed to Shimla from Bilaspur and Hamirpur to go via Barmana, Jukhala, Jwal Pul, Ranikotal, Gharsi, and Darlaghat. Vehicles travelling from Shimla toward Bilaspur and Hamirpur were suggested to proceed via Darlaghat, Gharsi, Ranikotal, Jwal Pul, and Ghumarwin/Barmana.

headline: Governor Gulab Chand Kataria Inaugurates Chandigarh's First-Ever Hunar Utsav.
content: Chandigarh, October 27, 2026:The Governor of Punjab and Administrator, U.T. Chandigarh, Shri Gulab Chand Kataria, today inaugurated Hunar Utsav 2026 – कौशल, संस्कृति, समृद्धि, the first-ever skill fest organised by the Department of School Education, Chandigarh Administration, at Sukhna Lake. The Administrator was accompanied by Shri Hiriadka Rajesh Prasad, Chief Secretary, U.T. Chandigarh, as Guest of Honour and Ms. Prerna Puri, Education Secretary; Shri Nitish Singla, Director School Education was also present during the inauguration. During his visit, the Administrator witnessed students showcasing their vocational skills, handcrafted products and creative work through a variety of stalls and interactive activities. The encouraging footfall and sales provided students with valuable exposure to customer interaction, product presentation and market demand, demonstrating how practical skills can translate into economic opportunities. Hunar Utsav provides students with a platform to demonstrate their vocational competencies, artistic talent and entrepreneurial abilities. The initiative aims to promote skill-based education, experiential learning and self-reliance by connecting classroom learning with practical applications. The festival features a diverse range of student-led stalls. Sui Dhaaga Kala showcases fashion creations and textile crafts, while Sajjaawat displays decorative products, including diyas, candles and torans. Roop Nikhar highlights beauty and wellness skills, Mehandi Ghar features mehndi designs, and Ink and Glam showcases nail art and tattoo artistry. Swaad Vatika presents culinary skills through food preparations and student-created delicacies. Promoting inclusion and lifelong learning, ‘Hum Kissi Se Kam Nahi’ highlighted the abilities and achievements of Children with Special Needs (CWSN), while ‘Ullas’ showcased initiatives related to Foundational Literacy and education. ‘Socho, Samjho, Jeeto’ featured skill-based games designed to encourage logical thinking and problem-solving skills among visitors. Hunar Utsav reflects the Chandigarh Administration’s commitment to holistic education that nurtures practical competencies, creativity, innovation and entrepreneurial thinking alongside academic learning. By showcasing and selling their creations, students gain hands-on experience while the festival promotes dignity and respect for craftsmanship and awareness of opportunities for self-employment.
